name: Synthetic Customer Complaint Handling
description: A hand-authored Phase 1 process used only to exercise the deterministic assessment contract. It is not an evaluation or benchmark case.
business_objective: Resolve complaints consistently and promptly while maintaining human accountability for consequential customer outcomes.

evidence.supporting_snippet: The service team receives approximately 1,200 complaints per month; about 85% arrive by email and agents manually re-key complaint details into the case system.
Most messages contain an order number, customer name, product, complaint category, and free-text description; agents verify extracted fields before a case is opened.
Two years of complaint emails and the corrected case fields are retained in an access-controlled case archive.
Cases are routed using a maintained table of product, region, and complaint-category rules; no contextual judgement is required when all three fields are present.
Agents consult the approved knowledge base, review the customer's history, and draft a response; an agent remains accountable for accuracy, tone, and any commitment made to the customer.
Incorrect advice can create customer detriment or regulatory complaints, but mandatory agent review before sending materially reduces the residual risk.
Management has proposed predicting customer churn, but the process description does not identify a historical churn outcome dataset, agreed labels, or a validated intervention pathway.
evidence.provenance: hand-authored synthetic statement of missing information

evidence.supporting_snippet: Regulated redress and compensation decisions depend on customer circumstances, legal obligations, precedent, and accountable manager sign-off; an incorrect decision can cause serious customer and regulatory harm.
The case system exposes controlled import and lookup interfaces, but any production integration would still require security, testing, and governance review.

steps.description: Read the incoming complaint, extract the core case fields, and assign an initial category before an agent verifies the result.

predictability.rationale: A stable set of fields and categories is used.

data_readiness.rationale: Historical messages and corrected fields are retained.

ai_capability_fit.rationale: Document extraction and classification directly match the activity.

human_judgement_requirement.rationale: Verification is required, but core extraction is structured.

business_value.rationale: The activity is frequent and currently requires manual re-keying.

risk_consequence.rationale: Incorrect fields can misroute a case but are checked before use.

residual_risk_with_human_oversight.rationale: Agent verification provides a strong control.

implementation_complexity.rationale: Controlled interfaces appear available, subject to later technical review.

conventional_solution_fit.rationale: Free-text interpretation is central, so fixed field rules alone fit poorly.

human_accountability_required.rationale: The agent verifies the extracted fields, but accountability for performing the extraction itself need not remain human.

steps.activity: Route the case to the responsible queue
steps.description: Use product, region, and category to route the verified case according to a maintained routing table.

data_readiness.rationale: The required verified fields and routing table already exist.

ai_capability_fit.rationale: Classification and workflow tools could perform routing, but AI is not required.

human_judgement_requirement.rationale: Complete cases require no contextual judgement.

business_value.rationale: Automated routing would remove a routine handling step.

risk_consequence.rationale: A routing error is recoverable through queue monitoring.

residual_risk_with_human_oversight.rationale: Existing exception queues can handle unmatched cases.

implementation_complexity.rationale: A maintained routing table and controlled interface already exist.

conventional_solution_fit.rationale: Deterministic rules directly encode the routing requirement.

human_accountability_required.rationale: Routing follows an approved deterministic table and exceptions remain visible.

steps.description: Retrieve approved guidance and draft a response for review and sending by an accountable agent.

repetition.rationale: A response is prepared for each complaint.

predictability.rationale: Approved guidance exists, but customer context varies.

data_readiness.rationale: The case, history, and approved knowledge are available.

ai_capability_fit.rationale: Knowledge retrieval and controlled drafting fit the task.

human_judgement_requirement.rationale: Context, tone, accuracy, and commitments require agent judgement.

business_value.rationale: Assistance applies across a high-volume activity.

risk_consequence.rationale: Incorrect advice can cause customer or regulatory detriment.

residual_risk_with_human_oversight.rationale: Mandatory review reduces but does not eliminate risk.

implementation_complexity.rationale: Knowledge and case interfaces appear available, subject to review.

conventional_solution_fit.rationale: Fixed templates cannot adequately handle the contextual drafting requirement.

human_accountability_required.rationale: An agent remains accountable for the response and commitments made.

steps.activity: Identify customers at risk of churn
steps.description: Estimate churn risk so that the service team can consider an appropriate retention intervention.

repetition.rationale: The proposal would apply to most complaint cases.

predictability.rationale: Prediction is plausible but outcome behaviour is not yet established.

data_readiness.rationale: No labelled historical churn outcome dataset is identified.

ai_capability_fit.rationale: Prediction could fit if a valid outcome and dataset are established.

human_judgement_requirement.rationale: A human would decide whether and how to intervene.

business_value.rationale: Retention may be valuable, but no measured opportunity is supplied.

risk_consequence.rationale: Poor predictions could produce unfair or inappropriate treatment.

residual_risk_with_human_oversight.rationale: Human intervention review may mitigate some risk.

implementation_complexity.rationale: Dataset, labels, model, intervention, and monitoring would need validation.

conventional_solution_fit.rationale: Simple rules may not capture future churn behaviour, but evidence is incomplete.

human_accountability_required.rationale: A human would remain accountable for deciding whether and how to intervene.

steps.description: Determine and authorise consequential compensation or redress using customer circumstances, obligations, and precedent.

repetition.rationale: Only a subset of complaints requires regulated redress.

predictability.rationale: Policy and precedent exist, but circumstances and obligations vary materially.

data_readiness.rationale: Case facts and policies exist, but relevant context may not be fully structured.

ai_capability_fit.rationale: Decision support is possible, but autonomous decision-making is inappropriate.

human_judgement_requirement.rationale: Expert contextual judgement and accountable sign-off are essential.

business_value.rationale: Consistent access to relevant information could help managers.

risk_consequence.rationale: Errors can cause serious customer, financial, legal, and regulatory harm.

residual_risk_with_human_oversight.rationale: The synthetic process states that the consequential decision itself must remain accountable and human-led.

implementation_complexity.rationale: Relevant information spans case, policy, and precedent sources.

conventional_solution_fit.rationale: Rules and workflow help but do not replace contextual judgement.

human_accountability_required.rationale: Authorised manager sign-off is explicitly required.
